facts.summary: InitDevice builds a std::vector<UINT> (push_back helper sub_c7b4c) on its stack, NOT a static array: default list {0xB100,0xB000,0xA100,0xA000,0x9300,0x9200,0x9100} (count 7, bytes written at 0x5bc288..0x5bc2ea). If byte [owner+0xbc]!=0 the vector is rebuilt as {0xB100,0xB000,0xA100,0xA000} (no 9_x) with Flags=0x20 and, when [owner+0xc4]!=0, DriverType=0 (UNKNOWN). Otherwise Flags=0, DriverType=1 (HARDWARE), pAdapter=NULL. On FAILED(hr) it Releases device/context and retries ONCE with DriverType=5 (WARP), same list/flags; the retry result is only logged (0x9d1058), a failure then crashes at 0x5bc406 (null context deref) - nothing checks it.

facts.summary: What the ARM D3D11CreateDevice hook must do: (1) flags |= 0x20 (BGRA); (2) replace the game's 7-entry list by the entries <= cap (default cap 0x9100 => exactly {0x9100}, count 1); (3) pass pFeatureLevel/ppDevice/ppContext through untouched (game relies on them); (4) on failure just return the HRESULT (game retries WARP itself via the same hook; WARP also supports 9_1). Verified offline: D3D11CreateDevice(levels={0x9100}) succeeds on hardware and WARP and returns selected=0x9100 / GetFeatureLevel=0x9100.

facts.summary: Advisable and cheap: accept --feature-level=9_1|9_2|9_3|10_0|10_1|11_0|11_1|game (+ env WIN32CRAFT_FEATURE_LEVEL), default 9_1 on ARM, 'game' = no clamp. Everything downstream (VERSION macro, target profile, vertex-format/sampler/colour paths) follows owner+0xb8 automatically, so no other host change is needed when the cap changes. Cap semantic: keep the game's own list order, drop entries > cap, if empty use {cap}. Examples: 9_1 -> {9100}; 9_3 -> {9300,9200,9100}; 10_0 -> {A000,9300,9200,9100}.

facts.summary: Source files are resolved by the game's resource system as 'shaders/hlsl/<name>.hlsl' ('/hlsl' 0x011b2080 + '.hlsl' 0x00dbcbf4 in sub_5c0ca8; first path component 'shaders' 0x00dc3ed0) from the material fields vertexShader/fragmentShader/vrGeometryShader/geometryShader ('shaders/renderchunk.vertex' etc.); includes come from the custom HeaderInclude object ('ShaderConstants.fxh', 'Util.fxh'/'util.fxh' both used - resolved case-insensitively by the game's file layer). There are NO per-FL variants: data/shaders contains hlsl/, glsl/, gnm/ and nine GUID-named override directories (7f4ba1a2..., 884ecfc8..., 98330b0a..., b8de1e1e..., bd49c9c7..., ce292d20..., d10c2615..., d1bea604..., d725e15d...) that each hold one replacement fragment shader (entity.fragment.hlsl; ce292d20 festive_foliage.fragment.hlsl) for specific resource packs. All 9 overrides also compile at ps_4_0_level_9_1. Material index files vanilla/materials/{common,fancy,sad}.json (and vanilla_base) list material files plus extra defines (FANCY, FOG, ALWAYS_LIT) and a tag suffix; materials use 'child:parent' inheritance.

facts.summary: Geometry shaders are only ever loaded for VR: all 111 'geometry' material keys are 'vrGeometryShader' (no 'geometryShader' key in any material, although the code also parses that key at 0x011bcae8). sub_5c0d58 loads the VR geometry shader only if *(0x15b86a4)+0xd (VR mode) is set, otherwise it clears the GS source (assign empty 0x10fbf90). A program with empty GS source makes compileShaderProgram return immediately (source size [this+0x68]==0) and the reflect step is skipped when [gs+0x31]==0 (0x5bd422) - so with FL<10 and non-VR NO geometry shader is compiled or created. 'gs_4_0_level_9_1' is not a valid target (tested X3506) and SV_InstanceID / SV_RenderTargetArrayIndex are rejected by the 9_x compilers (X4016), so VR/instanced-stereo cannot work at 9_1.

facts.summary: compileShaderProgram has an on-disk compiled-shader cache: after D3DPreprocess it hashes the preprocessed text (sub_9db99c), builds the file name <programName><hash-hex> (sub_8ce14) under a cache folder named 'ShaderCache2' (global string 0x00dbfc40, initialiser sub_4dbec; base folder from AppPlatform_Winrt 'cacheFolder'), reads it back (sub_9d3fb4 -> this+0x40) and only calls D3DCompile on a miss; on success it writes the blob (ostream::write at 0x5be724). The key does NOT include the target profile or FL: it is only the preprocessed source, which differs between FLs only where the source actually uses VERSION. A cache populated by a run at FL>=10 (plain vs_4_0/ps_4_0 blobs, or an x86 run) is therefore reused for shaders whose preprocessed text is FL-independent and then fails at CreateVertexShader/CreatePixelShader on a 9_x device (E_INVALIDARG, tested).
facts.x86_to_arm_notes: On ARM start with an empty cache; when the clamp/cap changes (or the build id changes) wipe '<cacheFolder>/ShaderCache2'. A simple host marker file 'ShaderCache2/fl_<cap>.txt' written on first run is enough.

port_instructions: 1. Replace install_d3d11_device_compat for ARM with a clamp hook on IAT cell 0x00C37A50 (VirtualProtect PAGE_READWRITE, write the hook's Thumb function pointer, FlushInstructionCache) installed BEFORE the call to the game's InitDevice (0x005BC258). Keep the x86 prototype: HRESULT WINAPI hook(void* adapter, UINT driver_type, HMODULE software, UINT flags, const UINT* levels, UINT count, UINT sdk_version, ID3D11Device** dev, UINT* selected, ID3D11DeviceContext** ctx). On ARM this is plain AAPCS (r0-r3 + 6 stack words).

2. Hook body (default cap 0x9100): `static UINT g_fl_cap = 0x9100; UINT out[8], n = 0; flags |= 0x20; if (g_fl_cap) { if (levels && count) for (i = 0; i < count && n < 8; ++i) if (levels[i] <= g_fl_cap) out[n++] = levels[i]; if (!n) out[n++] = g_fl_cap; levels = out; count = n; } hr = real_CreateDevice(adapter, driver_type, software, flags, levels, count, sdk_version, dev, selected, ctx); log hr + (selected ? *selected : 0); return hr;` With the game's list {B100,B000,A100,A000,9300,9200,9100} and cap 0x9100 this passes exactly {0x9100}, count 1. Do NOT touch pFeatureLevel (&owner[0xb8]) / ppDevice (&owner[0xc0]) / ppContext (&renderer[0x110]) - the game stores them itself and reads the level back only from owner+0xb8.

3. Do not implement host-side WARP retry: InitDevice itself retries once with DriverType=5 (WARP) through the same hook (0x5BC3EC) and WARP supports 9_1. But the game never checks the second result (null context => crash at 0x5BC406): after init_device() returns, check owner+0xc0 (device) and renderer+0x110 (context) for NULL exactly like initialize_game_d3d does and fail cleanly with a log line. Also log *(UINT*)(owner+0xb8) and expect 0x9100.

4. Override option: parse `--feature-level=<9_1|9_2|9_3|10_0|10_1|11_0|11_1|game>` and env WIN32CRAFT_FEATURE_LEVEL (value -> 0x9100,0x9200,0x9300,0xA000,0xA100,0xB000,0xB100; 'game' -> g_fl_cap = 0 = no clamp). Default on ARM = 9_1. The cap is the only knob: VERSION macro, shader target suffix, vertex formats, sampler filters and colour rounding all derive from owner+0xb8.

5. D3DCompile (IAT 0x00C370B4): NO text patches, NO include proxy on ARM. Keep an optional pass-through hook that, on FAILED(hr), logs source_name, target and the error blob (same prototype as the x86 win32_d3d_compile minus the include handling). Drop patch_hlsl_lod_intrinsic, patch_hlsl_root_signature, win32_include_*, shader_include_directory. The game already requests vs/ps_4_0_level_9_1 with VERSION=37120 once the device is 9_1; no profile override is needed.

6. Shader cache: the game keeps compiled blobs in <AppPlatform cacheFolder>/ShaderCache2 keyed by hash(preprocessed source) only (no FL/target in the key). Start ARM with an empty cache and wipe it whenever the effective FL cap changes (marker file e.g. ShaderCache2/fl_9100.txt) - blobs compiled for FL>=10 (plain 4_0/5_0) are rejected by FL9_1 devices (E_INVALIDARG).

7. Keep VR/stereo OFF: display descriptor stereo byte (+0x19)=0 (InitTargets would create an ArraySize-2 depth texture, invalid at 9_x), *(0x015B86A4)+0xd must stay 0, MSAA count (displaySettings+0xc) stays 1, TEXEL_AA (displaySettings+0x31) stays 0. Instanced/geometry-shader paths and 'SV_InstanceID' shaders do not compile at 9_1 (X4016).

8. Swap chain/targets (initialize_game_d3d): keep IDXGIFactory::CreateSwapChain B8G8R8A8_UNORM, BufferCount 2, DISCARD, windowed; clamp the client size used for the swap chain to <=2048 per axis (9_1/9_2 texture limit; 4096 for 9_3). Drop host_is_windows7 branches (BufferCount 1, RGBA fallback), patch_win7_*, captured_base_*. Keep install_scissor_fix (slot 45) and the Present hook (slot 8) unchanged.

9. Optional diagnostics: after InitDevice log owner+0xb8 and, via ID3D11Device::GetFeatureLevel (slot 37), the real level; call CheckFormatSupport for DXGI 87/28/37/45 to print a one-line capability summary (see arm32/tests/shader_probe.py --device for the exact calls).

10. Calling-convention note for all hooks: no thiscall/stdcall distinction on ARM; define hooks with WINAPI-less plain C signatures and make sure stack args are read as 4-byte values (UINT/pointers) in the exact order of fl91.createdevice_callsites / fl91.d3dcompile_call_args.
open_questions: Who (if anyone) sets GameOwner+0xbc (byte) to non-zero? Only make_owner (=0) writes it among owner users; non-zero would restrict the list to {B100..A000} and force FL>=10 - confirm no UWP path (HoloLens/VR) sets it on the host path.
Where exactly is [this+0x3f] (draw-call instance count) written? Assumed >1 only in instanced-stereo; not traced.

Real FL9_1 hardware behaviour (Tegra 3) could not be tested here: desktop drivers accept 4096 textures, R32 index buffers, NPOT+mips that the 9_1 spec restricts; ARM device logs are needed (use the D3DCompile/CreateDevice logging hooks).

ShaderCache2 base folder resolution (AppPlatform_Winrt::vf53 'cacheFolder') and whether the cache is also read before D3DPreprocess are only partially traced (read path via sub_9d3fb4 seen, write via ostream at 0x5be724).

Material 'defines' merge semantics for child:parent inheritance were assumed to be a union (the probe's 197 variants); an exact reproduction of MaterialDefinition flattening was not decompiled.
